full_judgment: 8. As regards the sale deed dated 19.09.1956, the trial Court found that although the plaintiffs claimed that the said kabala was fraudulent and collusive, they did not examine any witness to prove the said fact and the plaintiffs also failed to examine any witness to prove as to how forgery was committed in creating the said deed. The Appellate Court observed that since the plaintiffs claimed that the kabala dated 19.09.1956 was forged, the onus was upon them to prove the same as forged. The Appellate Court further observed that the kabala was a registered one and was 40 years old and in law, it had a presumption of correctness and thus it endorsed the view of the trial Court. We find nothing wrong with the view taken by the Courts below. In this regard, the High Court Division made a total wrong approach in observing that since PW1 deposed on his behalf and on behalf of the other plaintiffs that the alleged sale deed was forged and fraudulent as neither his sister nor he himself ever went to the office of Sub-Registrar and executed and registered the same, the onus was discharged by the plaintiffs that the deed in question was forged and fraudulent. And in the context, the learned Judge totally misconceived the provisions of section 103 of the Evidence Act.
